sentences.zh: 張融字思光，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Rong, styled Siguang, was a man of Wu in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rong, courtesy name Siguang, was a native of Wu in Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖褘，晉琅邪王國郎中令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hui was Director of Gentlemen of the Langye princedom under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhang Hui served as Director of Gentlemen of the Langye princedom under the Jin.

translations.literal: His father Chang was Administrator of Kuaiji under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang Chang was Administrator of Kuaiji under the Liu Song.

sentences.zh: 融年弱冠，道士同郡陸脩靜以白鷺羽麈尾扇遺融，曰：「此旣異物，以奉異人。

translations.literal: When Rong had just reached his twentieth year, the Daoist Lu Xiujing of the same commandery presented him with a fly-whisk fan of egret feathers, saying: "This is already a rare object; let it be offered to a rare man."
translations.idiomatic: While Rong was still in his early twenties, the Daoist Lu Xiujing of his home commandery gave him a fly-whisk fan made of egret feathers, saying, "This is no ordinary thing—it is fit for no ordinary man."

sentences.zh: 」宋孝武聞融有早譽，解褐爲新安王北中郎參軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Song heard that Rong had an early reputation and appointed him out of commoner status as Aide on the staff of the Prince of Xin'an's Northern Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Song heard of Rong's precocious renown, he appointed him from commoner status as an aide on the staff of the Prince of Xin'an's northern central army.

sentences.zh: 孝武起新安寺，僚佐多儭錢帛，融獨儭百錢。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu founded Xin'an Temple, his staff for the most part contributed money and silk, but Rong alone contributed a hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu founded Xin'an Temple, most of his staff contributed money and silk; Rong alone gave a hundred cash.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「融殊貧，當序以佳祿。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Rong is exceptionally poor; he should be ranked for a fine stipend."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Rong is desperately poor—he ought to be given a handsome salary."

translations.literal: He was sent out as Magistrate of Fengxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was then sent out to serve as magistrate of Fengxi.

sentences.zh: 從叔永出後渚送之，曰：「似聞朝旨，汝尋當還。

translations.literal: His paternal uncle Yong came out to Houzhu to see him off and said: "It seems I have heard the court's intent—you will soon return."
translations.idiomatic: His paternal uncle Zhang Yong came to Houzhu to see him off and said, "I hear the court intends to recall you before long."

sentences.zh: 」融曰：「不患不還，政恐還而復去。

translations.literal: Rong said: "I do not worry that I will not return; I only fear returning and then being sent away again."
translations.idiomatic: Rong replied, "I am not afraid I won't come back—I only fear coming back and being sent away again."

sentences.zh: 」廣越嶂嶮，獠賊執融，將殺食之，融神色不動，方作洛生詠，賊異之而不害也。

translations.literal: In the rugged barriers of Guang and Yue, Liao bandits seized Rong and were about to kill and eat him; Rong's expression did not change, and he was just then composing a Luoyang-style chant—the bandits marveled at him and did not harm him.
translations.idiomatic: In the steep passes of Guang and Yue, Liao bandits seized him and were about to kill and eat him. Rong's face never changed; he calmly recited in the Luoyang manner. The bandits were astonished and spared him.

sentences.zh: 浮海至交州，於海中作《海賦》曰：

translations.literal: He crossed the sea to Jiaozhou and on the ocean composed his "Rhapsody on the Sea," saying:
translations.idiomatic: He sailed to Jiaozhou and, on the open sea, composed his "Rhapsody on the Sea," which begins:

translations.literal: : The use of words is to give form to feeling.
translations.idiomatic: The purpose of language is to give shape to emotion.

sentences.zh: 使天形寅內敷，情敷外寅者，言之業也。

translations.literal: To make heaven's form spread inward and feeling spread outward—that is the work of words.
translations.idiomatic: When heaven's form unfolds within and feeling unfolds without, that is what words are meant to accomplish.

sentences.zh: 吾遠職荒官，將海得地，行關入浪，宿渚經波，傅懷樹觀，長滿朝夕，東西無里，南北如天，反覆懸烏，表裏菟色。

translations.literal: I hold a distant post in a wild office and take the sea as my domain; I pass through passes and enter waves, lodge on islets and traverse billows, cling to the shore and gaze at trees, long filled from dawn to dusk—east and west without measure, south and north like the sky, the hanging sun turning back and forth, inside and outside the hue of the hare.
translations.idiomatic: I serve far off in a remote post and take the sea as my domain. I cross passes and enter the breakers, lodge on sandbars and ride the swells, cling to the shore and watch the trees, filled from morning to night. East and west have no end; south and north are like the sky itself. The sun hangs and turns, and within and without all is the moon's pale color.

sentences.zh: 壯哉水之奇也，奇哉水之壯也。

sentences.zh: 故古人以之頌其所見，吾問翰而賦之焉。

translations.literal: Therefore the ancients sang what they saw in it; I asked my brush and made this rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients sang what they saw of it; I have asked my brush and composed this rhapsody.

sentences.zh: 當其濟興絕感，豈覺人在我外，木生之作，君自君矣。

translations.literal: When crossing stirs and feeling is cut off, how could one feel that others lie outside oneself? The work of Master Mu is your own affair.
translations.idiomatic: When the crossing stirs the spirit and feeling is cut away, how could one feel that others stand outside oneself? As for Master Mu's composition—that is your own affair.

translations.literal: Xuemo's son Zhan was chief clerk of the Prince of Nanyang's vanguard army; Rong submitted a petition asking to leave office, but permission was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Xuemo's son Zhan was chief clerk on the vanguard staff of the Prince of Nanyang; Rong submitted a petition asking to resign, but permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 融家貧願祿，初與從叔征北將軍永書曰：「融昔稱幼學，早訓家風，雖則不敏，率以成性。

translations.literal: Rong's family was poor and he desired a stipend; at first he wrote to his father's younger cousin, General who Campaigns North Yong, saying: "Rong was once praised for youthful study and early training in family tradition; though not sharp, by nature I have largely become what I am.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's family was poor and he wanted a salary; at first he wrote to his father's younger cousin, General who Campaigns North Zhang Yong, saying, "Rong was once praised for early study and upbringing in our family ways; though not clever, by temperament I have largely become what I am.

sentences.zh: 布衣葦席，弱年所安，簞食瓢飲，不覺不樂。

translations.literal: Plain cloth and reed mats—what I settled on in youth; basket of rice and gourd of drink—I feel neither lack nor sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Plain cloth and reed mats were what I made do with in youth; a basket of rice and a gourd of drink—I feel neither want nor unhappiness.

sentences.zh: 但世業清貧，民生多待，榛栗棗脩，女贄旣長，束帛禽鳥，男禮已大。

translations.literal: But the family's hereditary poverty left many lives waiting: hazelnuts, chestnuts, jujubes, and dried meat—the daughters' dowries were already grown; bundles of silk and bird offerings—the sons' marriage rites had already mounted.
translations.idiomatic: But our hereditary poverty leaves many lives waiting on me: hazelnuts, chestnuts, jujubes, and dried meat—the daughters' dowries have already grown heavy; bundles of silk and bird offerings—the sons' marriage rites have already grown costly.

sentences.zh: 勉身就官，十年七仕，不欲代耕，何至此事。

translations.literal: I force myself to take office; in ten years I have served seven times—not wishing to farm for others, how did it come to this?
translations.idiomatic: I force myself into office; in ten years I have taken seven posts—not wishing to live by another man's plow, how did it come to this?

sentences.zh: 昔求三吳一丞，雖屢舛錯。

translations.literal: Long ago I sought one assistant magistrate in the Three Wu districts, though repeatedly off the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago I sought a single assistant magistrate in the Three Wu region, though I was repeatedly passed over.

sentences.zh: 今聞南康缺守，願得爲之。

translations.literal: Now I hear the Administrator of Nankang is vacant and wish to obtain that post.
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear Nankang lacks an administrator, and I wish to obtain that post.

sentences.zh: 融不知階級，階級亦可不知，融政以求丞不得，所以求郡，求郡不得，亦可復求丞。

translations.literal: Rong does not know rank—and rank too may not know Rong; Rong just seeks an assistant magistrate and gets none, so seeks a commandery; if he cannot get a commandery, he may seek an assistant magistrate again.
translations.idiomatic: Rong does not know rank—and rank may not know Rong either; I sought an assistant magistrate and failed, so I seek a commandery; if I cannot get a commandery, I may seek an assistant magistrate again.

sentences.zh: 」又與吏部尚書王僧虔書曰：「融，天地之逸民也。

translations.literal: " He also wrote to Minister of the Civil Service Wang Sengqian, saying: "Rong is a recluse between Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: " He also wrote to Minister of the Civil Service Wang Sengqian, saying, "Rong is a recluse between Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 進不辨貴，退不知賤，兀然造化，忽如草木。

translations.literal: Advancing he does not distinguish the noble; withdrawing he does not know the base—still before creation, suddenly like grass or wood.
translations.idiomatic: Going forward he does not tell noble from common; stepping back he does not know high from low—he sits blank before creation, suddenly like grass or wood.

sentences.zh: 實以家貧累積，孤寡傷心，八姪俱孤，二弟頗弱，撫之而感，古人以悲。

translations.literal: Truly family poverty piles up and orphan widowhood wounds the heart: eight nephews all orphaned, two younger brothers quite weak—to nurture them moves one; the ancients wept over this.
translations.idiomatic: Truly poverty piles up at home and orphans and widows wound the heart: eight nephews all orphaned, two younger brothers quite frail—to raise them is moving; the ancients wept over such things.

sentences.zh: 豈能山海陋祿，申融情累。

translations.literal: How could mountain-and-sea paltry salary express Rong's emotional burdens?
translations.idiomatic: How could a paltry salary from some remote post express the burdens on Rong's heart?

sentences.zh: 阮籍愛東平土風，融亦欣晉平閑外。

translations.literal: Ruan Ji loved the soil and air of Dongping; Rong too delights in the leisure beyond Jinping.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Ji loved the country air of Dongping; Rong too delights in the quiet beyond Jinping.

translations.literal: " At the time opinion held that Rong lacked talent for governing the people, and in the end it did not happen.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time opinion held that Rong was no talent for governing people, and in the end he did not get the post.

sentences.zh: 辟太祖太傅掾，歷驃騎豫章王司空諮議參軍，遷中書郎，非所好，乞爲中散大夫，不許。

translations.literal: Recruited as a staff member in the Founder's Grand Tutor's office, he served as Remonstrance and Consultation Staff Officer under the Fast Cavalry General, Prince of Yuzhang, Bureau Director; was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman, but it was not to his liking, so he asked to become Regular Grand Master of the Palace—permission denied.
translations.idiomatic: He was recruited as a staff member in the Founder's Grand Tutor's office, served as Remonstrance and Consultation Staff Officer to the Fast Cavalry General, Prince of Yuzhang, Bureau Director, and was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman; it was not to his taste, so he asked to become Regular Grand Master of the Palace, but permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 融風止詭越，坐常危膝，行則曳步，翹身仰首，意制甚多。

translations.literal: Rong's carriage and deportment were eccentric and extraordinary: seated, he often perched on the edge of his knees; walking, he dragged his steps; he tilted his body and raised his head—his affectations were many.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's bearing was eccentric and outlandish: when seated he often perched on the edge of his knees; when walking he dragged his steps; he tilted his body and lifted his head—his mannerisms were many.

translations.literal: When he marched along per regulation with others, he was always slow and lagged behind.
translations.idiomatic: When he walked along with others as custom required, he was always slow and hung back.

sentences.zh: 太祖素奇愛融，爲太尉時，時與融款接，見融常笑曰：「此人不可無一，不可有二。

translations.literal: The Founder had always held Rong in special wonder and affection; when he was Grand Commandant he often received Rong warmly and, seeing him, would laugh and say: "This man—there cannot be none of him, and there cannot be two of him.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder had always regarded Rong with special wonder and affection; when he was Grand Commandant he often received Rong warmly and, seeing him, would laugh and say, "This man—there must be one of him, and there cannot be two.

sentences.zh: 」卽位後，手詔賜融衣曰：「見卿衣服麤故，誠乃素懷有本；

translations.literal: " After ascending the throne, he personally drafted an edict gifting Rong clothes, saying: "Seeing your clothes coarse and worn, this truly has roots in long-held simplicity;
translations.idiomatic: " After he took the throne, he personally drafted an edict gifting Rong clothes, saying, "Seeing your clothes coarse and worn, this truly springs from long-held simplicity;

translations.literal: Yet to meet you in tatters also diminishes the court's dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to receive you in tatters also diminishes the court's dignity.

sentences.zh: 今送一通故衣，意謂雖故，乃勝新也。

translations.literal: Now I send one set of old clothes, meaning that though old, they still surpass new.
translations.idiomatic: Now I send one set of old clothes, meaning that though they are old, they still surpass new ones.

sentences.zh: 是吾所著，已令裁減稱卿之體。

translations.literal: They are ones I wore; I have had them cut down to fit your frame.
translations.idiomatic: They are ones I wore myself; I have had them cut down to fit your frame.

translations.literal: Together with one pair of shoes."
translations.idiomatic: Together with one pair of shoes."

sentences.zh: 融與吏部尚書何戢善，往詣戢，誤通尚書劉澄。

translations.literal: Rong was on good terms with Minister of the Civil Service He Ji and went to visit Ji, but mistakenly entered the residence of Minister of the Secretariat Liu Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was on good terms with Minister of the Civil Service He Ji and went to visit him, but mistakenly entered the residence of Minister of the Secretariat Liu Cheng.

translations.literal: Rong alighted from his carriage and entered the gate, then said: "This is not it.
translations.idiomatic: Rong got down from his carriage and entered the gate, then said, "This is not it.

translations.literal: " Reaching the outer courtyard and seeing Cheng, he again said: "This is not it.
translations.idiomatic: " Reaching the outer courtyard and seeing Cheng, he again said, "This is not it.

translations.literal: " Once he had taken his seat and looked at Cheng, he said: "Altogether this is not it.
translations.idiomatic: " Once he had taken his seat and looked at Cheng, he said, "None of this is it at all.

translations.literal: " Then he left.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he left.

translations.literal: His eccentricity was like this.
translations.idiomatic: His eccentricity was like this.

sentences.zh: 又爲長沙王鎮軍、竟陵王征北諮議，竝領記室，司徒從事中郎。

translations.literal: He again served as Remonstrance and Consultation Staff Officer to the Prince of Changsha's Pacification Army and the Prince of Jingling's Northern Campaign Army, concurrently heading both secretariats, and as Attendant Gentleman in the Ministry of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as Remonstrance and Consultation Staff Officer on the Pacification Army staff of the Prince of Changsha and the Northern Campaign staff of the Prince of Jingling, concurrently heading both secretariats, and as Attendant Gentleman in the Ministry of Education.

translations.literal: , at the Zongming Hall he gave a lecture, and an edict ordered court officials to gather and listen.
translations.idiomatic: , he lectured at the Zongming Hall, and an edict ordered court officials to assemble and listen.

sentences.zh: 融扶入就榻，私索酒飲之，難問旣畢，乃長嘆曰：「嗚呼！

translations.literal: Rong was helped in and took his couch; he privately asked for wine and drank; when the difficult questions were finished, he sighed long and said: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Rong was helped in and took his couch; he privately asked for wine and drank; when the hard questions were finished, he sighed long and said, "Alas!

translations.literal: What sort of man was Confucius alone!
translations.idiomatic: What sort of man was Confucius, alone among men!

sentences.zh: 」爲御史中丞到撝所奏，免官，尋復。

translations.literal: " He was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Dao Hui, dismissed from office, and soon restored.
translations.idiomatic: " Censor-in-Chief Dao Hui impeached him; he was dismissed from office, and soon restored.

translations.literal: Rong's form and face were short and ugly; his spirit was clear and pure.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was short and ugly in appearance, yet clear and lucid in spirit.

sentences.zh: 王敬則見融革帶垂寬，殆將至骼，謂之曰：「革帶太急。

translations.literal: Wang Jingze saw Rong's leather belt hanging loose and wide, nearly reaching his hip bones, and said to him: "Your leather belt is too tight.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingze saw Rong's leather belt hanging loose and wide, nearly down to his hip bones, and said to him, "Your leather belt is too tight.

translations.literal: " Rong said: "Since I am not a foot messenger, why tighten the belt?"
translations.idiomatic: " Rong said, "Since I am not a foot messenger, why should the belt be tight?"

sentences.zh: 融假東出，世祖問融住在何處？

translations.literal: When Rong took leave to go east, Shizu asked where Rong lived.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong took leave to travel east, Emperor Shizu asked where Rong was living.

sentences.zh: 融答曰：「臣陸處無屋，舟居非水。

translations.literal: Rong answered: "Your servant on land has no house; living in a boat is not being on water.
translations.idiomatic: Rong answered, "Your servant on land has no house; living in a boat is not living on water.

sentences.zh: 」後日上以問融從兄緒，緒曰：「融近東出，未有居止，權牽小船，於岸上住。

translations.literal: " Later the Emperor asked Rong's father's elder brother's son Xu; Xu said: "Rong recently went east and had no fixed lodging; for the time being he had a small boat towed and stayed on the shore.
translations.idiomatic: " Later the emperor asked Rong's clansman Xu; Xu said, "Rong recently went east and had no fixed lodging; for the time being he had a small boat towed and stayed on the shore.

translations.literal: " The Emperor laughed aloud.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor laughed aloud.

sentences.zh: 虜中聞融名，上使融接北使李道固，就席，道固顧之而言曰：「張融是宋彭城長史張暢子不？

translations.literal: Among the northerners Rong's name was known; the Emperor had Rong receive the northern envoy Li Daogu. At table Daogu looked at him and said: "Is Zhang Rong the son of Zhang Chang, chief clerk of Pengcheng under Song, or not?
translations.idiomatic: Among the northerners Rong's name was known; the emperor had Rong receive the northern envoy Li Daogu. At table Daogu looked at him and said, "Is Zhang Rong the son of Zhang Chang, chief clerk of Pengcheng under Song, or not?

sentences.zh: 」融嚬蹙久之，曰：「先君不幸，名達六夷。

translations.literal: " Rong frowned and knit his brows a long while, then said: "My late father, alas—his name reached the Six Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong frowned and knit his brows a long while, then said, "My late father, alas—his name reached the Six Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 」豫章王大會賔僚，融食炙始行畢，行炙人便去，融欲求鹽蒜，口終不言，方搖食指，半日乃息。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang held a great gathering of guests and staff; Rong had just finished serving the roasted meat when the server left. Rong wanted salt and garlic but would not speak; he only wagged his index finger, and only after half a day did he stop.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yuzhang held a great gathering of guests and staff; Rong had just finished serving the roasted meat when the server left. Rong wanted salt and garlic but would not speak; he only wagged his index finger, and only after half a day did he stop.

sentences.zh: 出入朝廷皆拭目驚觀之。

translations.literal: Entering and leaving the court, all wiped their eyes and watched in astonishment.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he entered or left the court, people rubbed their eyes and stared in astonishment.

sentences.zh: 八年，朝臣賀衆瑞公事，融扶入拜起，復爲有司所奏，見原。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, when court officials congratulated the Emperor on auspicious omens, Rong was helped in to bow and rise; again he was impeached by the relevant offices and was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when court officials congratulated the emperor on auspicious omens, Rong was helped in to bow and rise; again the relevant offices impeached him, and he was pardoned.

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Education.

sentences.zh: 竟陵張欣時爲諸暨令，坐罪當死。

translations.literal: Zhang Xinshi of Jingling was magistrate of Zhuji; convicted of a crime, he faced death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xinshi of Jingling was magistrate of Zhuji; convicted of a crime, he was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 欣時父興世宋世討南譙王義宣，官軍欲殺融父暢，興世以袍覆暢而坐之，以此得免。

translations.literal: Xinshi's father Xingshi, when Song campaigned against the Prince of Nanqiao Xuan, the imperial army wished to kill Rong's father Chang—Xingshi covered Chang with his robe and sat on him, and by this Chang was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Xinshi's father Xingshi, when Song campaigned against the Prince of Nanqiao Xuan, the imperial army wished to kill Rong's father Chang; Xingshi covered Chang with his robe and sat on him, and by this Chang was spared.

sentences.zh: 興世卒，融著高履負土成墳。

translations.literal: When Xingshi died, Rong wore tall clogs and shouldered earth to build the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingshi died, Rong wore tall clogs and shouldered earth to build the tomb.

sentences.zh: 至是融啓竟陵王子良，乞代欣時死。

translations.literal: At this Rong submitted a memorial to the Prince of Jingling Xiao Ziliang, asking to die in Xinshi's stead.
translations.idiomatic: At this Rong submitted a memorial to the Prince of Jingling Xiao Ziliang, asking to die in Xinshi's place.

sentences.zh: 子良答曰：「此乃是長史美事，恐朝有常典，不得如長史所懷。

translations.literal: Ziliang answered: "This is indeed a fine act for a chief clerk—but I fear the court has fixed statutes and it cannot be as the chief clerk wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang answered, "This is indeed a fine act for a chief clerk—but I fear the court has fixed statutes, and it cannot be as the chief clerk wishes.

sentences.zh: 」遷黃門郎，太子中庶子，司徒左長史。

translations.literal: " He was promoted to Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, Household Supervisor of the Heir Apparent, and Left Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Education.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted to Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, Household Supervisor of the Heir Apparent, and Left Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Education.

sentences.zh: 融有孝義，忌月三旬不聽樂，事嫂甚謹。

translations.literal: Rong had filial devotion and righteousness: for the mourning month he abstained from music for thirty days and served his elder brother's wife with great care.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was filial and righteous: during the mourning month he abstained from music for thirty days and served his elder brother's wife with great care.

sentences.zh: 宋丞相義宣起事，父暢以不同將見殺，司馬竺超民諫免之。

translations.literal: When the Liu Song chief counsellor Xuan raised rebellion, his father Chang, because he did not agree, was about to be killed; Chief Administrator Zhu Chaomin remonstrated and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liu Song chief counsellor Xuan raised rebellion, his father Chang, because he did not agree, was about to be killed; Chief Administrator Zhu Chaomin remonstrated and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 暢臨終謂諸子曰：「昔丞相事難，吾緣竺司馬得活，爾等必報其子弟。

translations.literal: Chang on his deathbed told his sons: "In those days when the chief counsellor's affair was desperate, I lived thanks to Chief Administrator Zhu—you must repay his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Chang on his deathbed told his sons, "In those days when the chief counsellor's affair was desperate, I lived thanks to Chief Administrator Zhu—you must repay his descendants.

sentences.zh: 」後超民孫微冬月遭母喪，居貧，融往弔之，悉脫衣以爲賻，披牛被而反。

translations.literal: " Later Chaomin's grandson Wei encountered his mother's death in winter, lived in poverty; Rong went to condole, stripped off all his clothes as funeral gift, and returned wrapped in an ox hide.
translations.idiomatic: " Later Chaomin's grandson Wei suffered his mother's death in winter and lived in poverty; Rong went to condole, stripped off all his clothes as funeral gifts, and returned wrapped in an ox hide.

translations.literal: He always treated Wei as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: He always treated Wei as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 豫章王嶷、竟陵王子良薨，自以身經佐吏，哭輙盡慟。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yuzhang Yi and the Prince of Jingling Ziliang died, having himself served as their staff officer, he wept each time to the full limit of grief.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yuzhang Xiao Yi and the Prince of Jingling Xiao Ziliang died, having himself served as their staff officer, he wept each time to the full limit of grief.

translations.literal: , he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: , he died of illness.

translations.literal: He was fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 遺令建白旌無旒，不設祭，令人捉麈尾登屋復魂。

translations.literal: His final testament ordered a white banner without tassels, no sacrifices, and had someone grasp a fly-whisk, climb the roof, and call back the soul.
translations.idiomatic: His final testament ordered a white banner without tassels, no sacrifices, and had someone grasp a fly-whisk, climb the roof, and call back the soul.

sentences.zh: 曰：「吾生平所善，自當凌雲一笑。

translations.literal: It said: "What I favored all my life—naturally I shall laugh above the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: It said, "What I loved all my life—I shall naturally laugh above the clouds.

translations.literal: Three thousand [cash] for a coffin; do not make a new quilt.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand cash for a coffin; do not make a new quilt.

sentences.zh: 左手執《孝經》、《老子》，右手執小品《法華經》。

translations.literal: In the left hand hold the Classic of Filial Piety and the Laozi; in the right hand hold the summary version of the Lotus Sutra.
translations.idiomatic: In the left hand hold the Classic of Filial Piety and the Laozi; in the right hand hold the summary version of the Lotus Sutra.

sentences.zh: 妾二人，哀事畢，各遣還家。

translations.literal: The two concubines—when mourning is finished, send each back home.
translations.idiomatic: The two concubines—when mourning is finished, send each back home.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「以吾平生之風調，何至使婦人行哭失聲，不須暫停閨閤。」

translations.literal: " It also said: "Given the bearing of my whole life, why should women be made to walk and wail aloud? Do not have them pause even briefly in the inner chambers."
translations.idiomatic: " It also said, "Given the bearing of my whole life, why should women be made to walk and wail aloud? Do not have them pause even briefly in the inner chambers."

sentences.zh: 融玄義無師法，而神解過人，白黑談論，鮮能抗拒。

translations.literal: Rong's arcane doctrines had no master or method, yet his spiritual understanding surpassed others; in Dark-Light disputation few could resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's arcane doctrines had no master or method, yet his spiritual understanding surpassed others; in Dark-Light disputation few could stand against him.

sentences.zh: 永明中，遇疾，爲《門律自序》曰：「吾文章之體，多爲世人所驚，汝可師耳以心，不可使耳爲心師也。

translations.literal: In Yongming, when ill, he wrote "Preface to the Gate Rule," saying: "The style of my writings often startles the world—you may let the ear follow the heart, but must not let the ear be the heart's master.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongming, when ill, he wrote "Preface to the Gate Rule," saying, "The style of my writings often startles the world—you may let the ear follow the heart, but must not let the ear be the heart's master.

sentences.zh: 夫文豈有常體，但以有體爲常，政當使常有其體。

translations.literal: How could writing have a fixed form? Only to take having form as constant—that is precisely making the constant always have its form.
translations.idiomatic: How could writing have a fixed form? Only to take having form as constant—that is precisely making the constant always have its form.

sentences.zh: 丈夫當刪《詩》《書》，制禮樂，何至因循寄人籬下。

translations.literal: A man ought to abridge the Odes and Documents and formulate rites and music—why stoop to following old tracks and lodging under another's eaves?
translations.idiomatic: A man ought to abridge the Odes and Documents and formulate rites and music—why stoop to following old tracks and lodging under another man's eaves?

sentences.zh: 且中代之文，道體闕變，尺寸相資，彌縫舊物。

translations.literal: Moreover, writing of the middle ages lacks transformation of the Way's body; inch and foot complement each other, patching old stuff.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, writing of the middle ages lacks transformation of the Way's body; inch and foot complement each other, patching old stuff.

sentences.zh: 吾之文章，體亦何異，何嘗顛溫敘而錯寒暑，綜哀樂而橫歌哭哉？

translations.literal: My writing's form—how is it different? When did I ever invert warm narrative and misplace cold and heat, gather grief and joy and scatter song and weeping?
translations.idiomatic: My writing's form—how is it different? When did I ever invert warm narrative and misplace cold and heat, gather grief and joy and scatter song and weeping?

sentences.zh: 政以屬辭多出，比事不羈，不阡不陌，非途非路耳。

translations.literal: Precisely because phrasing goes many ways and parallel matters are unbound—not field-path not lane-path, not this road not that road.
translations.idiomatic: Precisely because phrasing goes many ways and parallel matters are unbound—not field-path, not lane-path, not this road, not that road.

sentences.zh: 然其傳音振逸，鳴節竦韻，或當未極，亦已極其所矣。

translations.literal: Yet its transmitting sound shakes and soars, its sounding cadences lift rhyme—perhaps not yet ultimate, yet already ultimate in its own reach.
translations.idiomatic: Yet its transmitting sound shakes and soars, its sounding cadences lift rhyme—perhaps not yet ultimate, yet already ultimate in its own reach.

sentences.zh: 汝若復別得體者，吾不拘也。

translations.literal: If you again find another form, I will not constrain you.
translations.idiomatic: If you again find another form, I will not constrain you.

sentences.zh: 吾義亦如文，造次乘我，顛沛非物。

translations.literal: My doctrine too is like my writing—sudden it takes me; in distress it is not a thing.
translations.idiomatic: My doctrine too is like my writing—sudden it takes me; in distress it is not a thing.

sentences.zh: 吾無師無友，不文不句，頗有孤神獨逸耳。

translations.literal: I have no teacher, no friends—not patterned, not claused—rather a lone spirit drifting alone.
translations.idiomatic: I have no teacher, no friends—not patterned, not claused—rather a lone spirit drifting alone.

sentences.zh: 義之爲用，將使性入清波，塵洗猶沐。

translations.literal: Doctrine's use will make nature enter clear waves, dust washed as if bathed.
translations.idiomatic: Doctrine's use will make nature enter clear waves, dust washed as if bathed.

sentences.zh: 無得釣聲同利，舉價如高，俾是道場，險成軍路。

translations.literal: Do not angle for renown in the same interest, hoist price as if high—lest this doctrinal ground become peril, a military road.
translations.idiomatic: Do not angle for renown in the same interest, hoist price as if high—lest this doctrinal ground become peril, a military road.

sentences.zh: 吾昔嗜僧言，多肆法辯，此盡遊乎言笑，而汝等無幸。

translations.literal: I once loved monks' words, often indulged in dharma debate—all play within speech and laughter, and you had no share of fortune.
translations.idiomatic: I once loved monks' words and often indulged in dharma debate—all play within speech and laughter, and you had no share of fortune.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「人生之口，正可論道說義，惟飲與食。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Human life's mouth—rightly may discuss the Way and expound doctrine; only drinking and eating
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "Human life's mouth—rightly may discuss the Way and expound doctrine; only drinking and eating

translations.literal: Beyond this is like a spiderweb in the trees.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond this is like a spiderweb in the trees.

sentences.zh: 吾每以不爾爲恨，爾曹當振綱也。」

translations.literal: I always regret not being so—you must uphold the main rope."
translations.idiomatic: I always regret not being so—you must uphold the main rope."

sentences.zh: 臨卒，又戒其子曰：「手澤存焉，父書不讀！

translations.literal: On nearing death he again admonished his sons: "The touch of a hand remains—and you will not read your father's writings!
translations.idiomatic: On nearing death he again admonished his sons, "The touch of a hand remains—and you will not read your father's writings!

translations.literal: How much more a father's tone and feeling, gracefully within its rhymes!
translations.idiomatic: How much more a father's tone and feeling, gracefully within its rhymes!

translations.literal: My intent is not so—I bequeath you my tone apart.
translations.idiomatic: My intent is not so—I bequeath you my tone apart.

sentences.zh: 吾文體英絕，變而屢奇，旣不能遠至漢魏，故無取嗟晉宋。

translations.literal: My literary style is heroically unique, transforming again and again with repeated marvels; since it cannot reach back to Han and Wei, I take no need to sigh over Jin and Song.
translations.idiomatic: My literary style is heroically unique, transforming again and again with repeated marvels; since it cannot reach back to Han and Wei, I take no need to sigh over Jin and Song.

translations.literal: Is it my heaven-bestowed excellence? Rather that I did not let the family's renown fall.
translations.idiomatic: Is it my heaven-bestowed excellence? Rather that I did not let the family's renown fall.

sentences.zh: 汝若不看，父祖之意欲汝見也。

translations.literal: If you do not read, the intent of father and grandfather was that you should see.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not read, the intent of father and grandfather was that you should see.

translations.literal: You may weep aloud as you read them.
translations.idiomatic: You may weep aloud over them as you read.

translations.literal: " Rong himself named his collected works Jade Sea.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong himself named his collected works "Jade Sea."

sentences.zh: 司徒褚淵問《玉海》名，融答：「玉以比德，海崇上善。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Chu Yuan asked about the name Jade Sea; Rong answered: "Jade compares to virtue; the sea exalts supreme goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Chu Yuan asked about the name "Jade Sea"; Rong answered, "Jade compares to virtue; the sea exalts supreme goodness.

translations.literal: " His collected writings, several tens of rolls, circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: " His collected writings, several tens of rolls, circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 張氏知名，前有敷、演、鏡、暢，後有充、融、卷、稷。

translations.literal: The Zhang clan was renowned; before were Fu, Yan, Jing, and Chang; after were Chong, Rong, Juan, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang clan was renowned: earlier generations included Fu, Yan, Jing, and Chang; later ones included Chong, Rong, Juan, and Ji.

translations.literal: Zhou Yong
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yong

sentences.zh: 周顒字彥倫，汝南安城人。

translations.literal: Zhou Yong, styled Yanlun, was a man of Ancheng in Ru'nan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yong, courtesy name Yanlun, was a native of Ancheng in Ru'nan.

sentences.zh: 晉左光祿大夫顗七世孫也。

translations.literal: He was the seventh-generation descendant of Yi, Left Minister of the Household under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He was the seventh-generation descendant of Zhou Yi, Left Minister of the Household under the Jin.

translations.literal: His grandfather Hutou was Attendant Outside Regular Service.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hutou served as Attendant Outside Regular Service.

translations.literal: His father Xun was Chancellor of Guixiang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xun served as Chancellor of Guixiang.

translations.literal: Yong in youth was recognized by his clansman and grandfather Lang.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Yong was recognized by his clansman and grandfather Zhou Lang.

translations.literal: Upon leaving commoner status, he became Gentleman Attendant of the Hailing princedom.
translations.idiomatic: Upon leaving commoner status, he became Gentleman Attendant of the Hailing princedom.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史蕭惠開賞異顒，攜入蜀，爲厲鋒將軍，帶肥郷、成都二縣令。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Yizhou Xiao Huikai admired Yong and took him into Shu, making him General Who Excites the Vanguard and concurrently magistrate of Feixiang and Chengdu counties.
translations.idiomatic: The Inspector of Yizhou Xiao Huikai admired Yong and took him into Shu, appointing him General Who Excites the Vanguard and concurrently magistrate of Feixiang and Chengdu counties.

sentences.zh: 轉惠開輔國府參軍，將軍、令如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to aide on Huikai's Pacification Army staff; his generalship and magistracies remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to aide on Huikai's Pacification Army staff, retaining his generalship and magistracies.

translations.literal: He then served as chief clerk of the princedom staff.
translations.idiomatic: He then served as chief clerk of the princedom staff.

sentences.zh: 常謂惠開性太險峻，每致諫，惠開不悅，答顒曰：「天險地險，王公設險，但問用險何如耳。

translations.literal: He often said Huikai's nature was too precipitous and harsh, and repeatedly remonstrated; Huikai was displeased and answered Yong: "Heaven has peril, earth has peril; lords and kings set peril—the question is only how peril is used.
translations.idiomatic: He often said Huikai's nature was too precipitous and harsh, and repeatedly remonstrated; Huikai was displeased and answered Yong, "Heaven has peril, earth has peril; lords and kings set peril—the question is only how peril is used.

translations.literal: " He returned to the capital with Huikai.
translations.idiomatic: " He returned to the capital with Huikai.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝頗好言理，以顒有辭義，引入殿內，親近宿直。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Song rather loved discourse on principle; because Yong had eloquence and meaning, he was brought into the palace halls and kept close on night watch.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Song was fond of discourse on principle; because Yong had eloquence and insight, he was brought into the palace halls and kept close on night watch.

sentences.zh: 帝所爲慘毒之事，顒不敢顯諫，輙誦經中因緣罪福事，帝亦爲之小止。

translations.literal: For cruel and poisonous things the emperor did, Yong dared not remonstrate openly but would recite sutra passages on karmic cause and retribution of sin and blessing, and the emperor would somewhat desist.
translations.idiomatic: For the cruel and vicious things the emperor did, Yong dared not remonstrate openly but would recite sutra passages on karmic cause and the retribution of sin and blessing, and the emperor would somewhat desist.

translations.literal: He was transferred to acting aide on the Pacification Army staff of the Prince of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to acting aide on the Pacification Army staff of the Prince of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 元徽初，出爲剡令，有恩惠，百姓思之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhui, he went out as magistrate of Shan; he showed kindness and favor, and the people missed him.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanhui era, he was appointed magistrate of Shan; he showed kindness and favor, and the people missed him when he left.

sentences.zh: 還歷邵陵王南中郎三府參軍。

translations.literal: Upon return he served successively as aide on the three staffs of the Prince of Shaoling, Southern Gentlemen-of-the-Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Upon returning to court he served successively as aide on the three staffs of the Prince of Shaoling, Southern Gentlemen-of-the-Palace.

translations.literal: When the Grand Progenitor assisted in government, he drew Yong in and received him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Progenitor assisted in government, he drew Yong in and received him.

sentences.zh: 顒善尺牘，沈攸之送絕交書，太祖口授令顒裁答。

translations.literal: Yong was skilled at letters; when Shen Youzhi sent a letter severing relations, the Grand Progenitor dictated orally and had Yong draft the reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was skilled at epistolary composition; when Shen Youzhi sent a letter severing relations, the Grand Progenitor dictated orally and had Yong draft the reply.

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant of the Qi headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Palace Attendant of the Qi headquarters.

sentences.zh: 建元初，爲長沙王參軍，後軍參軍，山陰令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan, he served as aide to the Prince of Changsha, aide on the Rear Army staff, and magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianyuan era, he served as aide to the Prince of Changsha, aide on the Rear Army staff, and magistrate of Shanyin.

translations.literal: The county had long registered pang households to supply miscellaneous labor.
translations.idiomatic: The county had long registered pang households to supply miscellaneous labor.

sentences.zh: 顒言之於太守聞喜公子良曰：「竊見滂民之困，困實極矣。

translations.literal: Yong spoke of this to the Administrator, Duke of Wenxi Xiao Ziliang: "I have privately seen the distress of pang households—it is truly at its limit.
translations.idiomatic: Yong spoke of this to the Administrator, Xiao Ziliang, Duke of Wenxi: "I have privately seen the distress of pang households—it is truly at its limit.

sentences.zh: 役命有常，祗應轉竭，蹙迫驅催，莫安其所。

translations.literal: Service orders have their quota, but tribute and response grow ever thinner; hounded and pressed, none can find rest.
translations.idiomatic: Service orders have their quota, yet tribute and response grow ever thinner; hounded and pressed, none can find rest.

sentences.zh: 險者或竄避山湖，困者自經溝瀆爾。

translations.literal: The desperate flee into mountains and lakes; the trapped hang themselves in ditches and drains.
translations.idiomatic: The desperate flee into mountains and lakes; the trapped hang themselves in ditches and drains.

sentences.zh: 亦有摧臂斮手，苟自殘落，販傭貼子，權赴急難。

translations.literal: Some smash arms or sever hands to mutilate themselves, sell themselves or indenture their children to meet sudden hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Some smash arms or sever hands to mutilate themselves, sell themselves or indenture their children to meet sudden hardship.

sentences.zh: 每至滂使發動，遵赴常促，輙有柤杖被錄，稽顙階垂，泣涕告哀，不知所振。

translations.literal: Whenever pang-service envoys were dispatched, deadlines were tight; there were always those in shackles taken for registration, prostrate with foreheads to the ground at the steps, weeping and pleading, not knowing what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever pang-service envoys were dispatched, deadlines were tight; there were always those in shackles taken for registration, prostrate with foreheads to the ground at the steps, weeping and pleading, not knowing what to do.

sentences.zh: 下官未嘗不臨食罷箸，當書偃筆，爲之久之，愴不能已。

translations.literal: This subordinate has never failed, upon facing a meal, to lay down chopsticks; when writing, to drop the brush—for long moments moved, unable to stop grieving.
translations.idiomatic: This subordinate has never failed, upon facing a meal, to lay down his chopsticks; when writing, to drop his brush—for long moments moved, unable to stop grieving.

sentences.zh: 交事不濟，不得不就加捶罰，見此辛酸，時不可過。

translations.literal: When labor exchanges failed, beatings had to be applied; seeing such bitterness, one could not bear to stay long.
translations.idiomatic: When labor exchanges failed, beatings had to be applied; seeing such bitterness, one could not bear to stay long.

translations.literal: In Shanyin's district administration, affairs were twice those of other cities;
translations.idiomatic: In Shanyin's district administration, affairs were twice those of other cities;

sentences.zh: 然略聞諸縣，亦處處皆躓。

translations.literal: yet from what I have heard, every county likewise stumbled everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: yet from what I have heard, every county likewise stumbled everywhere.

sentences.zh: 唯上虞以百戶一滂，大爲優足，過此列城，不無凋罄。

translations.literal: Only Shangyu, with one pang per hundred households, was greatly better off; beyond that tier of cities, none escaped depletion and exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shangyu, with one pang household per hundred households, was greatly better off; beyond that tier of cities, none escaped depletion and exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 宜應有以普救倒懸，設流開便，則轉患爲功，得之何遠。

translations.literal: There ought to be some means broadly to rescue those hanging upside down, to set flowing channels and open conveniences—then turning calamity into merit would be gained, how far off?
translations.idiomatic: There ought to be some means broadly to rescue those hanging upside down, to set flowing channels and open conveniences—then turning calamity into merit would be within easy reach.

sentences.zh: 」還爲文惠太子中軍錄事參軍，隨府轉征北。

translations.literal: " He returned as Chief Recording Aide on the Central Army staff of Crown Prince Wenxui; with the princedom he was transferred to Pacify-the-North.
translations.idiomatic: " He returned as Chief Recording Aide on the Central Army staff of Crown Prince Wenxui; with the princedom he was transferred to Pacify-the-North.

sentences.zh: 文惠在東宮，顒還正員郎，始興王前軍諮議。

translations.literal: When Wenxui was in the Eastern Palace, Yong returned as full Gentleman of the Palace and army staff counselor to the Prince of Shixing's Forward Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxui was in the Eastern Palace, Yong returned as full Gentleman of the Palace and army staff counselor to the Prince of Shixing's Forward Army.

translations.literal: He attended directly in the palace offices and again met with favor and esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He attended directly in the palace offices and again met with favor and esteem.

sentences.zh: 顒音辭辯麗，出言不窮，宮商朱紫，發口成句。

translations.literal: Yong's voice and diction were eloquent and lovely; words poured without end—tones like bell and chime, vermilion and purple—sentences formed at the opening of the mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's voice and diction were eloquent and lovely; words poured without end—tones like bell and chime, vermilion and purple—sentences formed at the opening of the mouth.

translations.literal: He ranged broadly through the hundred schools and excelled in Buddhist doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: He ranged broadly through the hundred schools and excelled in Buddhist doctrine.

translations.literal: He wrote Treatise on the Three Schools.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote "Treatise on the Three Schools."

translations.literal: He established emptiness of provisional names and non-emptiness of provisional names.
translations.idiomatic: He established emptiness of provisional names and non-emptiness of provisional names.

sentences.zh: 設不空假名難空假名，設空假名難不空假名。

translations.literal: Setting non-emptiness of provisional names to challenge emptiness of provisional names; setting emptiness of provisional names to challenge non-emptiness of provisional names.
translations.idiomatic: Setting non-emptiness of provisional names to challenge emptiness of provisional names; setting emptiness of provisional names to challenge non-emptiness of provisional names.

sentences.zh: 假名空難二宗，又立假名空。

translations.literal: Provisional-name emptiness challenged the two schools, and he further established provisional-name emptiness.
translations.idiomatic: Provisional-name emptiness challenged the two schools, and he further established provisional-name emptiness.

sentences.zh: 西涼州智林道人遺顒書曰：「此義旨趣似非始開，妙聲中絕六七十載。

translations.literal: The monk Zhilin of Western Liangzhou sent Yong a letter saying: "The meaning and purport of this doctrine seem not newly opened; the wondrous voice ceased midway for sixty or seventy years.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Zhilin of Western Liangzhou sent Yong a letter saying, "The meaning and purport of this doctrine seem not newly opened; the wondrous voice ceased midway for sixty or seventy years.

sentences.zh: 貧道年二十時，便得此義，竊每歡喜，無與共之。

translations.literal: This poor monk at age twenty already grasped this meaning, and secretly rejoiced each time, with no one to share it.
translations.idiomatic: This poor monk at age twenty already grasped this meaning, and secretly rejoiced each time, with no one to share it.

sentences.zh: 年少見長安耆老，多云關中高勝乃舊有此義，當法集盛時，能深得斯趣者，本無多人。

translations.literal: In youth I saw the elders of Chang'an; many said the eminent masters of Guanzhong already held this meaning; when dharma assemblies flourished, those who could deeply attain this purport were originally not many.
translations.idiomatic: In youth I saw the elders of Chang'an; many said the eminent masters of Guanzhong already held this meaning; when dharma assemblies flourished, those who could deeply attain this purport were originally not many.

translations.literal: After crossing the river to the east, there was roughly not one.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the river to the east, there was roughly not one.

sentences.zh: 貧道捉麈尾來四十餘年，東西講說，謬重一時，餘義頗見宗錄，唯有此塗白黑無一人得者，爲之發病。

translations.literal: This poor monk, grasping a flywhisk for forty-odd years, lecturing east and west, was wrongly esteemed for a time; other meanings appear much in sectarian records, but on this path alone neither lay nor clerical had one who attained it—I fell ill over it.
translations.idiomatic: This poor monk, grasping a flywhisk for forty-odd years, lecturing east and west, was wrongly esteemed for a time; other meanings appear much in sectarian records, but on this path alone neither lay nor clerical had one who attained it—I fell ill over it.

sentences.zh: 非意此音猥來入耳，始是眞實行道第一功德。

translations.literal: I did not expect this teaching unworthily to reach my ears—it is truly the first merit of genuine practice of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect this teaching unworthily to reach my ears—it is truly the first merit of genuine practice of the Way.

translations.literal: His treatise was thus esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: His treatise was thus esteemed.

sentences.zh: 顒於鍾山西立隱舍，休沐則歸之。

translations.literal: Yong built a hermitage west of Zhong Mountain and on rest days returned to it.
translations.idiomatic: Yong built a hermitage west of Zhong Mountain and on rest days returned to it.

sentences.zh: 轉太子僕，兼著作，撰起居注。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Steward of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Compiler, compiling the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Palace Steward of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Compiler, compiling the Veritable Records.

translations.literal: He was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman, retaining his concurrent post as Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman, retaining his concurrent post as Compiler.

translations.literal: He often attended and served in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He often attended and served in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 少從外氏車騎將軍臧質家得衞恒散隷書法，學之甚工。

translations.literal: In youth from his mother's clan, in General of Chariots and Cavalry Zang Zhi's household, he obtained Wei Heng's draft clerical script and studied it to great mastery.
translations.idiomatic: In youth, from his mother's clan in General of Chariots and Cavalry Zang Zhi's household, he obtained Wei Heng's draft clerical script and studied it to great mastery.

sentences.zh: 文惠太子使顒書玄圃茅齋壁，國子祭酒何胤以倒薤書求就顒換之，顒笑而答曰：「天下有道，丘不與易也。」

translations.literal: Crown Prince Wenxui had Yong write on the walls of the thatched study in the Mystic Enclosure; the National University Rector He Yin sought to exchange his inverted-leek script for Yong's, and Yong smiled and replied: "When the realm has the Way, Qiu would not trade for it."
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Wenxui had Yong write on the walls of the thatched study in the Mystic Enclosure; the National University Rector He Yin sought to exchange his inverted-leek script for Yong's, and Yong smiled and replied, "When the realm has the Way, Qiu would not trade for it."

sentences.zh: 每賔友會同，顒虛席晤語，辭韻如流，聽者忘倦。

translations.literal: Whenever guests and friends gathered, Yong would leave an empty seat for intimate talk; phrasing and tone flowed like water, and listeners forgot weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever guests and friends gathered, Yong would leave an empty seat for intimate talk; phrasing and tone flowed like water, and listeners forgot weariness.

sentences.zh: 兼善老、易，與張融相遇，輙以玄言相滯，彌日不解。

translations.literal: He was also skilled in Laozi and the Changes; meeting Zhang Rong, they would detain each other with arcane discourse, not parting for whole days.
translations.idiomatic: He was also skilled in Laozi and the Changes; meeting Zhang Rong, they would detain each other with arcane discourse, not parting for whole days.

sentences.zh: 清貧寡欲，終日長蔬食，雖有妻子，獨處山舍。

translations.literal: Poor and pure, with few desires, all day long he ate vegetables; though he had wife and children, he lived alone in a mountain lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Poor and pure, with few desires, all day long he ate vegetables; though he had wife and children, he lived alone in a mountain lodge.

sentences.zh: 衞將軍王儉謂顒曰：「卿山中何所食？

translations.literal: General of the Guard Wang Jian said to Yong: "In the mountains, what do you eat?
translations.idiomatic: General of the Guard Wang Jian said to Yong, "In the mountains, what do you eat?

translations.literal: " Yong said: "Red rice and white salt, green mallow and purple smartweed.
translations.idiomatic: " Yong said, "Red rice and white salt, green mallow and purple smartweed.

sentences.zh: 」文惠太子問顒：「菜食何味最勝？

translations.literal: " Crown Prince Wenxui asked Yong: "Among vegetable foods, which flavor is finest?
translations.idiomatic: " Crown Prince Wenxui asked Yong, "Among vegetable foods, which flavor is finest?

translations.literal: " Yong said: "Early leeks at spring's first flush; late cabbages at autumn's end.
translations.idiomatic: " Yong said, "Early leeks at spring's first flush; late cabbages at autumn's end.

translations.literal: " At the time He Yin also devoutly practiced Buddhism and had no wife or concubine.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time He Yin also devoutly practiced Buddhism and had no wife or concubine.

sentences.zh: 太子又問顒：「卿精進何如何胤？

translations.literal: The Crown Prince again asked Yong: "How does your religious devotion compare with He Yin's?
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince again asked Yong, "How does your religious devotion compare with He Yin's?

translations.literal: " Yong said: "The three evil destinies and eight difficulties—neither of us has escaped them.
translations.idiomatic: " Yong said, "The three evil destinies and eight difficulties—neither of us has escaped them.

translations.literal: Yet each has his own burden.
translations.idiomatic: Yet each has his own burden.

translations.literal: He was transferred to Erudite of the National University, retaining his concurrent post as Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Erudite of the National University, retaining his concurrent post as Compiler.

sentences.zh: 太學諸生慕其風，爭事華辯。

translations.literal: The university students admired his style and vied in ornate disputation.
translations.idiomatic: The university students admired his style and vied in ornate disputation.

sentences.zh: 後何胤言斷食生，猶欲食肉、白魚、脯、糖蟹，以爲非見生物。

translations.literal: Later He Yin said he had renounced eating living things, yet still wished to eat meat, white fish, cured meat, and sugared crab, holding that these were not creatures seen alive.
translations.idiomatic: Later He Yin said he had renounced eating living things, yet still wished to eat meat, white fish, cured meat, and sugared crab, holding that these were not creatures seen alive.

translations.literal: Uncertain about eating clams and oysters, he had the students debate it.
translations.idiomatic: Uncertain about eating clams and oysters, he had the students debate it.

sentences.zh: 學生鍾岏曰：「之就脯，驟於屈伸，蟹之將糖，躁擾彌甚。

translations.literal: The student Zhong Yan said: "When it becomes cured meat, the rush of bending and stretching is sudden; when a crab meets sugar, its agitation is all the worse.
translations.idiomatic: The student Zhong Yan said, "When it becomes cured meat, the rush of bending and stretching is sudden; when a crab meets sugar, its agitation is all the worse.

translations.literal: A humane person's intent would be deeply pained, as if afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: A humane person's intent would be deeply pained, as if afflicted.

sentences.zh: 至於車螯蚶蠣，眉目內闕，慚渾沌之奇，礦殼外緘，非金人之慎。

translations.literal: As for razor clams and oysters, eyes and brows are inwardly lacking—they would be ashamed before Chaos's marvel; mineral shells sealed without, unlike the golden man's caution.
translations.idiomatic: As for razor clams and oysters, eyes and brows are inwardly lacking—they would be ashamed before Chaos's marvel; mineral shells sealed without, unlike the golden man's caution.

sentences.zh: 不悴不榮，曾草木之不若；

translations.literal: Neither withering nor flourishing—they are not even like grass and trees;
translations.idiomatic: Neither withering nor flourishing—they are not even like grass and trees;

sentences.zh: 無馨無臭，與瓦礫其何算。

translations.literal: without fragrance or stench—what difference from rubble?
translations.idiomatic: without fragrance or stench—what difference from rubble?

sentences.zh: 故宜長充庖廚，永爲口實。

translations.literal: Thus they ought ever to fill the kitchen and forever serve as tidbits.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they ought ever to fill the kitchen and forever serve as tidbits.

translations.literal: " When Xiao Ziliang, Prince of Jingling, saw Yan's disputation, he was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: " When Xiao Ziliang, Prince of Jingling, saw Yan's disputation, he was greatly angered.

translations.literal: Yin's elder brother Dian also withdrew to purity and devout faith.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's elder brother He Dian also withdrew to purity and devout faith.

translations.literal: Yong wrote him a letter urging him to eat vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: Yong wrote him a letter urging him to eat vegetables.

sentences.zh: 曰：「丈人之所以未極遐蹈，或在不近全菜邪？

translations.literal: He said: "The reason you, sir, have not yet reached the utmost distant practice may lie in your not coming close to a fully vegetable diet, may it not?
translations.idiomatic: He said, "The reason you, sir, have not yet reached the utmost distant practice may lie in your not coming close to a fully vegetable diet, may it not?

sentences.zh: 脫灑離析之討，鼎俎網罟之興，載之簡策，其來寔遠。

translations.literal: The debates of shedding constraints and dissecting distinctions, the rise of cauldrons, stands, nets, and traps recorded in bamboo and silk—their coming is indeed far off.
translations.idiomatic: The debates of shedding constraints and dissecting distinctions, the rise of cauldrons, stands, nets, and traps recorded in bamboo and silk—their coming is indeed far off.

translations.literal: Who would dare to intervene in debate?
translations.idiomatic: Who would dare to intervene in debate?

sentences.zh: 觀聖人之設膳脩，仍復爲之品節，蓋以茹毛飲血，與生民共始，縱而勿裁，將無厓畔。

translations.literal: Observing how the sage set out meals and provisions, he still graded and regulated them—for eating raw flesh and drinking blood began together with the birth of the people; if indulged without restraint, there would be no margin or limit.
translations.idiomatic: Observing how the sage set out meals and provisions, he still graded and regulated them—for eating raw flesh and drinking blood began together with the birth of the people; if indulged without restraint, there would be no margin or limit.

sentences.zh: 善爲士者，豈不以恕己爲懷？

translations.literal: One who is good at being a gentleman—would he not take putting oneself in another's place as his intent?
translations.idiomatic: One who is good at being a gentleman—would he not take putting oneself in another's place as his intent?

sentences.zh: 是以各靜封疆，罔相陵軼。

translations.literal: Thus each keeps quiet within his borders and does not encroach upon or overrun another.
translations.idiomatic: Thus each keeps quiet within his borders and does not encroach upon or overrun another.

sentences.zh: 況乃變之大者，莫過死生；

translations.literal: Moreover, among great transformations, none surpasses death and life;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, among great transformations, none surpasses death and life;

translations.literal: among what living values, nothing exceeds life and fate.
translations.idiomatic: among what living values, nothing exceeds life and fate.

sentences.zh: 性命之於彼極切，滋味之在我可賒，而終身朝晡，資之以永歲，彼就冤殘，莫能自列，我業久長，吁哉可畏。

translations.literal: Life and fate to them is utmost urgent; flavor to me can be deferred—yet lifelong, morning and evening, I rely on them to sustain the year; they meet wrongful slaughter and mutilation, unable to plead for themselves, while my karma grows long-lasting—alas, how dreadfully fearsome.
translations.idiomatic: Life and fate to them is utmost urgent; flavor to me can be deferred—yet lifelong, morning and evening, I rely on them to sustain the year; they meet wrongful slaughter and mutilation, unable to plead for themselves, while my karma grows long-lasting—alas, how dreadfully fearsome.

sentences.zh: 且區區微卵，脆薄易矝，歂彼弱麑，顧步宜衄。

translations.literal: Moreover tiny eggs, fragile and thin, easily crushed; suckling fawns at every step would rightly blush.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover tiny eggs, fragile and thin, easily crushed; suckling fawns at every step would rightly blush.

sentences.zh: 觀其飲喙飛沈，使人憐悼，況可心心撲褫，加復恣忍吞嚼。

translations.literal: Watching them drink and peck, fly and sink, moves one to pity—how much less to chase them down heart by heart, stripping and flaying them, then further indulging cruel swallowing and chewing.
translations.idiomatic: Watching them drink and peck, fly and sink, moves one to pity—how much less to chase them down heart by heart, stripping and flaying them, then further indulging cruel swallowing and chewing.

sentences.zh: 至乃野牧盛羣，閉豢重圈，量肉揣毛，以俟枝剝，如土委地，僉謂常理，可爲愴息，事豈一塗。

translations.literal: Extending even to vast herds in open pasture, penned and fattened in layered enclosures, measuring flesh and gauging hide to await butchering and flaying—as if dirt cast to earth, all call it ordinary reason; one could sigh in grief—the matter is surely not of one kind alone.
translations.idiomatic: Extending even to vast herds in open pasture, penned and fattened in layered enclosures, measuring flesh and gauging hide to await butchering and flaying—as if dirt cast to earth, all call it ordinary reason; one could sigh in grief—the matter is surely not of one kind alone.

sentences.zh: 若云三世理誣，則幸矣良快，如使此道果然，而受形未息，則一往一來，一生一死，輪迴是常事。

translations.literal: If one says the doctrine of the three ages is deception, then fortunate indeed and truly relieved; but if this Way is real and rebirth in form has not ceased, then going forth and returning, living once and dying once—transmigration is ordinary business.
translations.idiomatic: If one says the doctrine of the three ages is deception, then fortunate indeed and truly relieved; but if this Way is real and rebirth in form has not ceased, then going forth and returning, living once and dying once—transmigration is ordinary business.

sentences.zh: 雜報如家，人天如客，遇客日尠，在家日多，吾儕信業，未足長免，則傷心之慘，行亦自及。

translations.literal: Mixed retribution is like being at home; human and heavenly rebirths are like being a guest—days as guest are few, days at home are many; we who trust in karma are not long exempt, and the heart-breaking misery will in time reach us as well.
translations.idiomatic: Mixed retribution is like staying at home; rebirths in human and heavenly realms are like lodging as a guest—guest days are few, home days are many. We who trust in karma cannot escape for long, and heart-breaking misery will reach us in turn.

sentences.zh: 丈人於血氣之類，雖無身踐，至於晨鳧夜鯉，不能不取備屠門。

translations.literal: You, sir, toward creatures of blood and breath, though you do not personally go to the slaughter, as for morning duck and night carp, you cannot but have them prepared at the butcher's gate.
translations.idiomatic: Though you do not yourself visit the slaughterhouse, sir, you still cannot do without morning duck and night carp from the butcher's gate.

sentences.zh: 財貝之一經盜手，猶爲廉士所棄；

translations.literal: Wealth that has once passed through a thief's hands is still cast away by an upright man;
translations.idiomatic: Wealth that has once passed through a thief's hands is still cast away by an upright man;

sentences.zh: 生性之一啓鸞刀，寧復慈心所忍。

translations.literal: yet when living flesh meets the imperial cleaver, how could a compassionate heart bear it?
translations.idiomatic: yet when living flesh meets the cleaver, how could a compassionate heart bear it?

sentences.zh: 騶虞雖飢，非自死之草不食，聞其風豈不使人多愧。

translations.literal: Though the Zouyu is hungry, it will not eat grass that has not died of itself—hearing of its spirit, should it not make one deeply ashamed?
translations.idiomatic: Though the Zouyu is hungry, it will not eat grass that has not died of itself—hearing of its spirit, should it not make one deeply ashamed?

sentences.zh: 衆生之稟此形質，以畜肌膋，皆由其積壅癡迷，沈流莫反，報受穢濁，歷苦酸長，此甘與肥，皆無明之報聚也。

translations.literal: All living beings who receive this bodily form to store flesh and fat do so from accumulated obstruction, delusion, and confusion, sinking in the stream without return, receiving defiled retribution, passing through long bitterness and sourness—this sweetness and richness are all aggregates of retribution born of ignorance.
translations.idiomatic: All beings who receive this bodily form to store flesh and fat do so from accumulated delusion, sinking in the stream without return, receiving defiled retribution through long bitterness—this sweetness and richness are all aggregates of ignorance's retribution.

sentences.zh: 何至復引此滋腴，自汙腸胃。

translations.literal: Why go further and draw this rich nourishment to defile one's own bowels?
translations.idiomatic: Why then draw this rich nourishment to defile one's own bowels?

translations.idiomatic: When Yong died in office, Wang Jian had not yet finished lecturing on the Classic of Filial Piety; Yong recommended Tanji to succeed him, and the scholars honored the choice.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：弘毅存容，至仁表貌，汲黯剛戇，崔琰聲姿，然後能不憚雄桀，亟成譏犯。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: With resolute forbearance and stored composure, with utmost benevolence showing in one's bearing, with Ji An's blunt integrity and Cui Yan's voice and presence—only then can one not fear powerful bullies and quickly become a target of censure.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Only with resolute forbearance, utmost benevolence in bearing, Ji An's blunt integrity, and Cui Yan's voice and presence can one not fear powerful bullies and quickly become a target of censure.

sentences.zh: 張融標心託旨，全等塵外，吐納風雲，不論人物，而干君會友，敦義納忠，誕不越檢，常在名教。

translations.literal: Zhang Rong marked his heart and entrusted his purpose, wholly equal to what lies beyond the dust; he breathed in and out wind and cloud and did not discuss persons—yet in serving his lord and meeting friends he was earnest in righteousness and loyal submission, never overstepping propriety, always within the teaching of names.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rong marked his heart and entrusted his purpose, wholly beyond the dust of the world; he breathed wind and cloud and cared nothing for persons—yet in serving his lord and meeting friends he was earnest in righteousness and loyalty, never overstepping propriety, always within the bounds of moral teaching.

sentences.zh: 若夫奇偉之稱，則虞飜、陸績不得獨擅於前也。

translations.literal: As for the title of singular and grand, Yu Fan and Lu Ji cannot monopolize it in earlier times.
translations.idiomatic: As for the reputation of singular greatness, Yu Fan and Lu Ji cannot monopolize it among those who came before.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：思光矯矯，萬里千仞。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Siguang towers aloft, ten thousand li and a thousand ren high.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: Siguang towers aloft, ten thousand li and a thousand ren high.

translations.literal: Promoted, he harmonized with those who answered; dismissed, he parted with those who were cast away.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted, he harmonized with those who answered; dismissed, he parted with those who were cast away.

translations.idiomatic: His aim lay in horizontal alliances, not in plotting to break seals.
